transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess I'm just having a really hard time lately. Ever since my daughter left for basic training, it’s like... I feel like I come home to a dead house. I just can’t keep myself together. 

It’s affecting my job. I'm sitting there crying in my truck before my shifts even start. I'm missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, which isn't like me, and I keep snapping at the younger guys on the crew. And when I'm home... I've stopped going out on the water or working on my sculpture. I just don’t see the point right now. I figured I needed to come in before things get any worse.
Do you feel these problems started because your daughter left for basic training?
Yeah, I really do. I was managing just fine before she shipped out. But all of this... it just started within a few weeks of her actually leaving for basic training.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel down or depressed all day, every day. It's more just... when I'm alone in the house, or when I have too much time to think about her being gone. There are times at work where I'm focused and feeling okay, but then it just hits me again. So it's not a constant, everyday kind of depression, no.
Have you been feeling hopeless?

No, I don't think hopeless is the right word. I know she's coming back, and I know things will eventually get easier. It's just... really hard right now. But I haven't lost hope or anything like that.
Have you had any thoughts of killing yourself?
No. No, definitely not. I mean... it's been really tough with her being gone, like I said, but I haven't had any thoughts like that. I would never do something like that.
Have you been feeling especially anxious or nervous since your daughter left?

Not really, no. I mean, I worry about her being on her own, just like any mom would, but I wouldn't say I feel anxious or nervous. It's not a panicky feeling or anything like that. It's really just... feeling the emptiness of the house more than anything else. So no, no real anxiety.
Since your daughter left, have you noticed a big change in your sleep?

No, my sleep is pretty much the same. I mean... I'm usually pretty tired by the end of the day from work, so I fall asleep alright. I haven't really had any trouble staying asleep, either. It's just waking up and realizing she's not in the next room... that part is hard. But the actual sleeping part is fine. I haven't noticed any big changes there.
Since your daughter left, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Since she left for basic training... I just feel like I come home to a dead house. I can’t seem to keep myself together. I used to love going out on the water, or working on my metal sculptures, but I’ve completely stopped doing all of that. I just don’t see the point right now. 

It's honestly bleeding into everything else, too. I'm sitting in my truck crying before my shifts even start. At work, I'm missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and I keep snapping at the younger guys on the crew. I just don't have the energy or the interest for much of anything lately.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?

No, not really. I mean, I'm tired after work, but that's normal for me. It's a physical job, so I'm always a bit worn out by the time I clock out. But I wouldn't say it's an unusual kind of tired, or like I have no energy overall. It's just the normal amount of tired.
Would you say this has significantly interfered with your ability to function at work?

Yeah, it really has. Like I was saying about missing steps earlier... my supervisor actually took me off a complex welding job recently. He told me I just wasn't coordinating safely enough to be doing it right now, and he's probably right. My head just isn't in it. And it's not just my day job, either. I had a deadline for a sculpture submission that I just let pass by without finishing the piece. I just can't seem to focus or get things done like I usually do.
Have these symptoms been going on for at least two weeks?
Yeah, it's been longer than that. It's been about a month since she left, and... well, I've pretty much been struggling like this ever since then.
Since your daughter left, have you noticed any change in your appetite?
No, not really. I'm eating about the same as I usually do. I haven't noticed any major changes there.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
Well, yeah, like I mentioned a minute ago, I'm definitely having trouble focusing. My head just isn't in it, and I'm missing steps at work. It's just hard to keep my mind on what I'm doing right now.
Before your daughter left for basic training, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt like this for at least two weeks?
No, I haven't. I mean, I've had stressful days before, like anyone, but... no. I've never felt this down or out of it for weeks on end. This is really the first time it's been like this.
Lately, have you been feeling worthless or overly guilty?
No, not really. I don't feel worthless or anything like that. And I don't feel guilty either. I'm just having a really hard time with her being gone, but it's not guilt. I just miss her.
